clue.text: Go to pieces as rent's increased

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split, so a crack
prices that are up have increased

explanation.surface: A tenant falls apart on hearing that the rent has gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up is an idiom for breaking down mentally, falling apart emotionally.

clue.text: Reject belief in bird losing weight then adding weight

indicators.note: after the loss, a further piece is tacked on at the end
the bird is said to lose something, so a letter is dropped from its name

parts.note: a wren is a small bird
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone loses faith in a bird that shed a little weight and then put some back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes W from WREN, leaving REN.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce a creed or faith is formally to give up and abandon one's commitment to it.

clue.text: In conflict about flogging

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
lashing is whipping, a flogging

explanation.surface: Two parties are at odds over the use of corporal punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Clashing describes things that collide or disagree, so at odds with one another.

clue.text: Mark's after articles from France and Germany, getting stress

indicators.note: the mark is said to come after the articles, so its letters follow them

parts.note: UN is a French indefinite article
DER is a German definite article
a score is a mark, as in a test result

explanation.surface: A teacher's mark is followed by foreign grammar lessons, causing pupils stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To underscore something is to emphasise or highlight it, literally by underlining.

clue.text: Graphic symbol of swindler's confession?

definitions.meaning: a small picture on a screen standing for a program or file
a con man owning up would say '...'

explanation.surface: A picture represents a fraudster owning up to his trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer screen pictogram that stands for an app or file is this kind of image.

clue.text: Lay out trendy underwear

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
a vest is an undergarment in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone shows off fashionable underclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to lay out money, spending it in hope of a return.

clue.text: One of the family runs into trouble

indicators.note: the runs are put into the trouble, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: bother means trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A relative keeps getting into difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling is a family member, so a male sibling fits.

clue.text: Bid of £100 raised by end

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred pounds
the rump is the hind end

explanation.surface: An auction bid of a hundred pounds is increased at the close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TON into NOT. A no-trump bid is a call in the card game bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a no-trump call is a contract played with no trump suit.

clue.text: Outline in which one car is overturned

indicators.note: the car is turned over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of a crash in which a vehicle flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a sketch or synopsis of how events might unfold, a plot outline.

clue.text: Grandee adopted defensive stance

indicators.note: the letters are taken on in a new form, adopted into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A nobleman took up a guarded posture.
explanation.walkthrough: EN GARDE is the fencing call to take up the guard position.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing, this French term names the guard posture taken before a bout.

clue.text: Cares not about one farther up the tree

indicators.note: about can mean around or turned, so these letters are moved round

explanation.surface: Someone shows indifference towards a person higher up in the branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear sits higher on a family tree than those descended from them.

clue.text: Cut off a date line when travelling

indicators.note: the letters move about as if on a journey, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crossing the International Date Line leaves a traveller disconnected.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone alienated feels estranged, isolated and cut off from others.

clue.text: Creator of a ramshackle hut finished with gold

indicators.note: the gold comes at the end, finishing the word
a ramshackle building is tumbledown, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A builder makes a rickety shed and tops it off with gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer is the creator or originator of a work.

clue.text: Escape outpouring that follows passing of coach perhaps

definitions.text: that follows passing of coach perhaps

parts.note: to slip away is to escape
a stream is a flow, an outpouring

explanation.surface: A gush of air trails behind a bus as it goes by.
explanation.definitionFit: The current of air behind a fast-moving vehicle trails in its wake.

clue.text: Second Catholic's disposed to be concerned with education

indicators.note: disposed can mean arranged, so these letters are set out afresh

parts.note: the word with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A second churchgoer is inclined towards teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges CATHOLICS into CHOLASTIC; the 's of the clue supplies a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholastic means relating to schools and learning, so academic.

clue.text: Old Bob is able to look at something quickly

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated S
can means is able

explanation.surface: An elderly man named Bob can glance at things fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is not a person: a bob was a pre-decimal British shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a page is to skim or glance over it rapidly.

clue.text: American native whose day always seems the same?

definitions.meaning: a North American burrowing rodent, the woodchuck

definitions.text: whose day always seems the same?
definitions.meaning: The film where one day repeats endlessly

explanation.surface: A Native American lives a monotonous life.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodchuck is a marmot native to North America, celebrated each February.

clue.text: Incline to fail, interrupting scholarship perhaps

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: a grant is an award like a scholarship
to die is to fail, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: A student fears flunking will cut off their funding.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, an incline on a road or hill.

clue.text: Part of shoe damaged — it's a blow

parts.note: the upper is the top part of a shoe
cut means damaged, wounded

explanation.surface: A ruined shoe is described as a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's upward punch to the chin is a kind of blow.

clue.text: Glossy coat to go missing, worn by Romeo

indicators.note: Romeo is worn, so covered, by the other piece

parts.note: to vanish is to disappear
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A shiny jacket disappears, having been worn by a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A varnish is a clear shiny finish brushed onto wood.

clue.text: Player putting key in a lock

indicators.note: the key goes in, so it is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone inserts a key into a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' is hair, not a door fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress plays roles on stage, so she is a player.

clue.text: Artillerymen's pints carried away

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
PT is the abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: Gunners' beers are taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means enraptured, so entranced and transported with delight.

clue.text: Nice cat lad gets befuddled — it's not intended

indicators.note: befuddled means confused, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A boy from Nice and his cat get confused, but it was unintentional.
explanation.definitionFit: An accidental event happens by chance, unplanned and unintentional.

clue.text: Reread novel that's more treasured

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh form

explanation.surface: Rereading a book makes it more precious.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearer is the comparative of dear, meaning loved or cherished.

clue.text: Count governed in a daze

parts.note: to add is to count up
led means governed or directed

explanation.surface: A nobleman who ruled was confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled means muddled or confused, unable to think clearly.

clue.text: Told of French beginning to take Scottish isle, suffering complete reverse

indicators.note: the whole assembly undergoes reversal, so it is read from the end

parts.note: DE is French for of

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word gives its first letter

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: A tale of a Frenchman starting to capture an island and then being routed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering complete reverse' turns the whole string DETARRAN round, not just one piece. Arran is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrated means recounted as a story, so told.

clue.text: Otherwise gripped by Handel's 'Esther'

indicators.note: the letters are held within the run of these words

explanation.surface: A different idea appears in a Handel oratorio.
explanation.definitionFit: Else means otherwise, as in 'or else'.

clue.text: Increase prison sentence

definitions.meaning: slang for a term in jail

explanation.definitionFit: A stretch means both an extension and slang for jail time.

clue.text: State of uncertainty caused by southern coppers reportedly holding American

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the American inside them
reportedly signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: pennies are coppers, so pence

explanation.surface: Uncertainty arises when southern police detain an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' are coins, not police. PENSE sounds like PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is anxious uncertainty while awaiting an outcome.

clue.text: Film expert standing in front of gallery

indicators.note: the expert comes first, before the gallery

parts.note: an ace is an expert
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A specialist waits outside an art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulose acetate was used as photographic film base.
